questions.q: What does an Identification Rule actually decide?
options: Which CI class a record belongs to
How often Discovery should run against a given CI class
Which source wins when two sources disagree on a field
Which attributes, in combination, prove two incoming records describe the same real-world asset
questions.explain: Identification is about recognizing duplicates before they're created, not about resolving conflicting field values.

questions.q: Why is matching a server CI on Name alone a weak identification approach?
options: ServiceNow technically forbids using the Name field for matching
Name fields are always encrypted and unreadable to Identification Rules
Name matching is actually the strongest possible approach
Name is a display label a human typed, not a stable, reliable identifier
questions.explain: A real identification rule relies on attributes like serial number or Host Name + Domain, which are far harder to accidentally duplicate or mistype.

questions.q: What is the difference between an independent and a dependent identifier?
options: An independent identifier is reliable on its own (serial number); a dependent identifier only proves a match in combination with another attribute (Host Name + Domain)
There is no real difference between the two terms
Dependent identifiers are always more reliable than independent ones
Independent identifiers only apply to network CIs
questions.explain: A hostname alone isn't unique across domains, but paired with Domain it usually is -- that's what makes it dependent rather than independent.

questions.q: What does a Reconciliation Rule decide that an Identification Rule does not?
options: Whether two records describe the same physical asset
Which data source's value wins on a specific field when multiple sources disagree
How many relationships a CI should have
Which CI class a new record should be created in
questions.explain: Reconciliation only matters once Identification has already confirmed two records are the same CI -- then it resolves field-level conflicts.

questions.q: Why is 'whichever source wrote most recently wins' a dangerous default for reconciliation?
options: Recent writes are always more accurate than older ones in every case
It only affects CI classes that don't use Discovery at all
It lets a stale or incorrect import silently overwrite good, freshly-discovered data, with no field-level logic protecting it
ServiceNow does not allow this behavior to occur under any configuration
questions.explain: An authoritative-source rule, designated per field, protects correct data from being overwritten regardless of which system happened to write last.
